claims.text: A plan to make a custom Firefox with a Ruflo hive of Claude Code workers, an sgit vault as its memory and a behaviour policy as its mandate, for the laptop and the iPad.
claims.quote: a plan to make a custom Firefox with the workflow we showed at the agentics talk

claims.text: The workflow is a hive, a memory and a mandate: Ruflo gives the hands, an sgit vault the memory, and an Agent Behaviour Policy gives each role its mandate.
claims.quote: a hive, a memory and a mandate

claims.text: The plan is a proposal that the owner has not run yet, and it says so where it matters.
claims.quote: The plan below is a proposal: I have not run it yet

claims.text: The plan starts as explorer coding: the owner writes the wants in his own words, the list goes into the vault, and it is the brief.
claims.quote: That list goes into the vault, and it is the brief.

claims.text: For each want the first worker finds the lowest layer that delivers it, because every layer up is more to maintain.
claims.quote: for each want, find the lowest layer that delivers it, because every layer up is more to maintain

claims.text: Firefox reads a policies.json from a distribution folder; policies cover menus, home page, search, extensions and the AI sidebar, survive updates and need almost no maintenance.
claims.quote: They survive updates and need almost no maintenance.

claims.text: A userChrome.css in the profile can restyle or hide any part of the browser's interface; it is the most powerful layer without code and the least stable, because it is unsupported.
claims.quote: It is the most powerful layer without code, and the least stable

claims.text: Extensions need to be signed by Mozilla, an unlisted one is signed and then distributed by the owner, and extensions cannot restructure the browser.
claims.quote: They cannot restructure the browser.

claims.text: A personal fork is a small patch set on top of the release, the way LibreWolf carries 63 patches and Debian 17, applied to each new version.
claims.quote: carries 63 patches and Debian 17, applied to each new version

claims.text: Firefox's artifact mode downloads pre-built C++ components, so a change to the interface does not need the full compile.
claims.quote: downloads pre-built C++ components rather than building them locally

claims.text: A full Firefox build is within reach on a laptop: Mozilla asks for 8 GB of memory and 30 GB of disk.
claims.quote: 8 GB of memory and 30 GB of disk

value.unit: GB of memory for a full build, with 30 GB of disk

claims.text: Mozilla's trademark policy forbids distributing a modified Firefox under that name, so a personal fork has to be renamed; only Mozilla can ship a custom build called Firefox.
claims.quote: you may not distribute a modified form of Firefox and continue to call it Firefox

claims.text: Apple's App Review Guideline 2.5.6 requires apps that browse the web to use WebKit, with exceptions only in the EU and Japan.
claims.quote: Apps that browse the web must use the appropriate WebKit framework

claims.text: Mozilla has decided not to build Gecko for iOS because a separate build would mean doubling the size of its iOS team.
claims.quote: would mean we would basically have to double the size of our iOS team

claims.text: Firefox for iOS is a separate Swift codebase on WebKit, none of the desktop layers exist there, and the only route is a fork built in Xcode and installed on the owner's iPad.
claims.quote: The only route is a fork of that codebase, changed by the hive, built in Xcode and installed on my own iPad.

claims.text: With a free Apple account the install lasts 7 days on up to 3 devices; a paid developer account gives a year and TestFlight.
claims.quote: the install lasts 7 days

value.unit: days an install lasts with a free Apple account

claims.text: The maintenance loop: each Firefox release starts a run in which the hive rebases the patches, rebuilds, tests each want, compares screenshots and reports, and the owner approves or refuses.
claims.quote: the hive rebases the patches, rebuilds, tests each want, compares screenshots and reports

claims.text: Since Firefox 155 on 1 September a new major release is made every two weeks, so a fork has 26 releases a year to follow, on each of two codebases.
claims.quote: so a fork has 26 releases a year to follow, on each of two codebases

claims.text: LibreWolf, with a team, ships within three days of each upstream release; Waterfox's maintainer describes a project often run by one person and a few months in the red.
claims.quote: a few months in the red recently

claims.text: The behaviour policy says what no worker may do: change anything but the front end, weaken security, updates or signing, use Mozilla's trademarks, or ship without the owner's approval.
claims.quote: change anything but the front end, weaken security, updates or signing, use Mozilla's trademarks, or ship without my approval

claims.text: PortGPT, a research system for porting Linux patches to older versions, reported an 89.15% success rate on 1,815 cases.
claims.quote: a research system for porting Linux patches to older versions, reported

claims.text: The owner found no browser fork maintained without people checking the result, so the plan has him read the report and approve every release.
claims.quote: I read the report and approve every release

claims.text: Mozilla should sell to one person what it sells to organisations: explore for free, keep it working for about 50p a release, a change built properly for £50 to £500.
claims.quote: I think it should sell the same to one person

claims.text: On 12 October Mozilla introduced Firefox Enterprise, with its own branding and a management console, and its paid support offers custom development options.
claims.quote: On 12 October it introduced

claims.text: Keeping a customisation tested against each release at about 50p a release comes to £13 a year.
claims.quote: That is £13 a year.

value.unit: GBP a year at about 50p a release

claims.text: Mozilla is better placed than the owner to keep a custom Firefox working: it alone can ship a modified build called Firefox, it signs extensions, it builds the next release and it maintains both codebases.
claims.quote: Mozilla is better placed than I am

claims.text: Mozilla depends on royalties for about three quarters of its revenue, and charging per version or per change is the income its chief executive meant by diversifying beyond search.
claims.quote: the kind of income its chief executive meant by

claims.text: The plan has not been run; every step is checked against the documentation, not tried end to end.
claims.quote: It is a plan; every step is checked against the documentation, not tried end to end.

claims.text: The prices are illustrative, the owner's and not Mozilla's.
claims.quote: The prices are illustrative. Mine, not Mozilla's.

claims.text: Mozilla's consumer offer does not exist; its enterprise build and support do, and their prices are not public.
claims.quote: Its enterprise build and support do; their prices are not public.

claims.text: No agent maintains a browser fork alone; the plan keeps a person approving every release.
claims.quote: No agent maintains a browser fork alone.

claims.text: The iPad route needs a developer account and only changes what Firefox for iOS can change on WebKit.
claims.quote: The iPad route needs a developer account.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of the owner on 16 October 2026, written by the site's agent in the voice of the site.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 16 October 2026
